Hi team — quick ops assessment after reviewing the traffic profile and doing a sizing pass: see attached ops-estimate.xlsx (summary tab). TL;DR: feasible with two viable approaches.

Option A — Dedicated reserved pool (recommended for strict guarantees):
- Reserved GPU cluster colocated in us-west-2 with prioritized routing for /recs.
- Estimated additional capacity: 8x A100-equivalent slots (based on peaks in attachment).
- Expected p95: ~80-110ms with KV caching + continuous batching tuned for 1–3 token responses.
- Risk: warm-up periods and cold-starts for new shards; need warm standby and pre-warming policy.
- Cost delta (ballpark): +$85k/month.

Option B — Hosted priority lanes + smart routing (faster to spin up, lower cost):
- Use existing hosted infrastructure with dedicated priority queues and aggressive prefix KV caching.
- Expected p95: ~110-140ms depending on burst pattern; risk of variance under unexpected traffic spikes.
- Cost delta (ballpark): +$25k–40k/month, but less predictable SLA in tail cases.

Operational asks for either option:
- 24/7 on-call escalation contact for first 90 days (SRE rotation).
- Canary rollouts and synthetic tests that exercise the /recs path every 3 minutes.
- Trace-level retention for 7 days and token-level cost telemetry exposed to GalaxyCore dashboards.

Suggested contractual language (draft):
- Commitment: p95 latency <= 120ms during defined window; uptime 99.95% for the route.
- Remedy: operational credit (additional support hours + prioritized capacity adjustments) for incidents; monetary credits only for repeated SLA breaches (>=3 breaches in 90 days).

I’ve attached ops-estimate.xlsx and a sample redwood_dedicated_config.json for the dedicated pool. Happy to run numbers tighter in the deep-dive tomorrow.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
